tasks.short: Help managers and employees sort out contract questions and problems at work.

today.trigger: A manager or employee raises a question through Outlook, Teams, or a conversation at Rotterdam, Tilburg, or Venlo.
steps: Listen to the issue and establish what the person needs.
Find the relevant AFAS contract, SharePoint policy, and applicable CAO provisions.
Check the facts with the manager, employee, HR Administrator, or Payroll Specialist.
Explain the position and discuss a practical resolution with those involved.
Record agreed actions and follow up until the issue is resolved.
drudgery: Asking repeatedly for missing dates, contract details, and earlier correspondence.
Reconstructing a case from scattered email threads.
Chasing agreed actions and writing similar follow-up messages.
today.time_sinks: Repeated fact finding and follow-up interrupt conversations that need attention. This is an assumed workflow for the fictional company, rather than an observed baseline.

lenses.faster: An intake form and a source-linked case brief remove repeated requests for facts and most email reconstruction. The HRBP starts the conversation with the relevant records and unresolved questions.
lenses.autonomous: New requests create a restricted case, identify missing information, and schedule follow-up reminders. Routine policy questions go to the shared policy service; disputes and personal interpretation come to the HRBP.
lenses.ambitious: Give every new starter a clear route to raise problems during the first 90 days, including employees on night shifts. Resolve small problems before they become reasons to leave.
lenses.joy: Remove thread searching, duplicate notes, and reminder chasing. Keep listening, building trust, and helping people reach an agreement.
lenses.options: Prepare several possible resolutions with their contract implications, practical costs, and questions still unanswered. The HRBP checks which options are fair and workable.
lenses.altitude: Own the quality of issue resolution: recurring causes, escalation rules, response times, and whether agreed actions actually helped.
reach: HR Administrator: structured intake and case completeness checks.
Payroll Specialist: identify which contract or pay facts need specialist review.
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: define anonymised issue categories and resolution measures.

tasks.human_edge: Employees need someone who hears their account, challenges management when necessary, and takes responsibility for a fair resolution. Mediation, discipline, and consequential contract interpretations remain human work.
tasks.pattern_why: copilot for case briefs, questions, and draft follow-ups; deterministic_software for routing and reminders. keep_human applies to mediation and decisions affecting employment.

in_practice.trigger: An employee or manager submits a request, or the HRBP records an issue raised in person.
steps: Create a restricted case and offer immediate human contact for urgent or sensitive matters.
Request only the missing information needed and route ordinary policy questions to the policy service.
Retrieve authorised contract and policy records and draft a dated brief separating facts, allegations, and gaps.
The HRBP hears the relevant people, checks the brief, and decides how to proceed.
Draft agreed actions for HRBP approval and send rule-based reminders against approved deadlines.
in_practice.human_gate: The HRBP approves personal advice, case notes, communications, and closure. Threats, harassment, disciplinary matters, and contested facts receive direct human handling.
systems: AFAS Profit through a scoped read-only connection or approved export
Power Automate and an approved enterprise LLM, proposed additions requiring access and licence checks
data_needed: Relevant contract and employment dates.
Applicable CAO and current policy versions.
Case-specific correspondence supplied or authorised for this purpose.
Case owner, agreed actions, and deadlines.
Access permissions and retention rules; medical diagnoses excluded.
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint case register: source references, draft versions, human corrections, approvals, and action status. Approved employment records go into AFAS where appropriate.

evidence.claim: IBM reports that Ask HR handles over 11 million interactions annually, with approximately 180 HRBPs handling complex escalations. This supports a routine-service and human-escalation model, not automated mediation.
The Dutch privacy regulator distinguishes employer-held absence information from medical information held by the bedrijfsarts.
The 30% labour saving and 1.2 times elapsed speed are untested planning assumptions; conversations and waiting for people remain.

risks: A generated brief can turn an allegation into an apparent fact or omit the employee's account.
Broad mailbox access could expose unrelated personnel information; restrict retrieval to the authorised case.
Wet verbetering poortwachter deadlines require approved rules and a named owner; AI cannot assess medical fitness.
Routine questions must remain easy to escalate, including for shift workers without reliable Teams access.
Count policy interpretation savings under the separate policy task; this estimate covers intake, preparation, and follow-up.
research_questions: What share of this task is fact finding and follow-up, rather than conversations and judgment?
Can AFAS and SharePoint access be limited to the exact records each case handler may see?
Do shift workers and flex workers have a usable route to a person during all operating shifts?
Does a pilot reduce days to resolution without increasing reopened cases or reducing employee trust?

tasks.short: Explain which HR policy or CAO rule applies and what someone needs to do next.

today.trigger: Someone asks about leave, contracts, allowances, absence procedures, or another HR rule.
steps: Establish the relevant employment category, site, and date.
Find the current SharePoint policy, CAO provision, or approved legal guidance.
Check whether exceptions or conflicting provisions affect the answer.
Explain the rule in plain language and describe the next step.
Refer personal disputes or specialist questions to the appropriate human owner.
drudgery: Answering the same policy question many times.
Finding the correct document version.
Rewriting formal provisions into understandable instructions.
today.time_sinks: The answer often depends on the applicable CAO and effective date, while documents and earlier explanations are scattered.

lenses.faster: Retrieve the applicable approved clause and produce a short explanation with a source link. Repeated searching and rewriting disappear for established questions.
lenses.autonomous: Answer tested categories of general policy questions when they arrive, including outside office hours. Escalate conflicting sources, missing eligibility information, and individual legal interpretation.
lenses.ambitious: Provide clear policy explanations in the languages employees actually use across all shifts. Turn unanswered questions into a queue for improving the policy library.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive explanations and document hunting. Keep the difficult interpretation and the conversation where someone needs reassurance or advocacy.
lenses.options: Offer a short answer, a worked example, or a step-by-step explanation using the same approved rule. Compare relevant provisions when more than one employment category is possible.
lenses.altitude: Design and maintain the policy service: document ownership, applicability rules, test questions, escalation routes, and answer quality.
reach: HR Administrator: routine policy enquiries and form guidance.
Compensation and Benefits Specialist: explain approved allowance and benefit rules.
Learning and Development Specialist: distribute approved policy learning materials.

tasks.human_edge: The HRBP owns ambiguous interpretations and situations where a technically correct answer could still be unfair or misleading.
tasks.pattern_why: llm_step turns an approved provision into plain language inside a deterministic workflow that selects sources, checks applicability, and routes exceptions. No model is needed for eligibility calculations whose rules can be written explicitly.

in_practice.trigger: An employee or manager asks a policy question through an approved channel.
steps: Disclose that the service uses AI and collect only the context needed to select the applicable rules.
Use approved applicability rules to select current CAO and policy sources; verify agency-worker arrangements separately.
Retrieve relevant clauses and generate an answer containing source links, effective dates, and the next action.
Release answers only within tested topics with sufficient sources; otherwise create a human escalation.
Sample released answers and feed corrections into the owned source library and regression tests.
in_practice.human_gate: Policy owners approve sources, applicability rules, and automated topics before release. The HRBP approves exceptions, disputes, and consequential personal advice; new personnel-data arrangements require the applicable OR process.
systems: Teams and an approved mobile-accessible channel
AFAS Profit for narrowly scoped applicability attributes where necessary
Microsoft Copilot Studio and Power Automate, proposed additions with licensing and integration to verify
data_needed: Current CAO texts and Noordhaven policies with owners and effective dates.
Approved applicability and exception rules.
Only necessary attributes such as employment category and site.
Approved FAQs and reviewed test questions.
Agency-specific guidance identifying the employer and applicable terms.
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint service register: topic, source versions, answer, escalation reason, and reviewer corrections, with personal content minimised and an approved retention period.

evidence.claim: Coca-Cola Andina's Copilot Studio HR assistant provides contextual answers and creates human escalation tickets. Microsoft reports 1,200 monthly users and CSAT of 4.1 out of 5.
evidence.source: [S4: Microsoft Learn, Coca-Cola Andina HR support case](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/guidance/case-studies/coca-cola-andina-hr-support)

evidence.claim: Personnel-data arrangements and employee-monitoring provisions are subject to OR consent rights under WOR article 27(1)(k)/(l); OR consent does not itself establish GDPR compliance.
Article 50 requires people to be informed when interacting with AI unless this is already obvious.
The 65% labour saving and 2 times elapsed speed assume substantial routine volume, maintained sources, and usable employee access; they are not case-study results for Noordhaven.

risks: The service may apply the transport CAO to a warehouse employee or Noordhaven terms to an agency employee.
Expired documents or incorrect effective dates can produce convincing but wrong advice.
Answers about individual rights can cross from general explanation into legal interpretation.
An AI answer must not change AFAS entitlements, contracts, or payroll records.
AVG/GDPR requires a lawful basis, limited access, processor arrangements, and a DPIA where processing is likely to create high risk.
research_questions: What percentage of enquiries can be answered from approved sources without personal interpretation?
Can document owners maintain reliable versions and applicability rules for both CAOs and agency arrangements?
Does a reviewed test set show correct answers and reliable escalation across employment categories and languages?
Will frontline employees use the service, and what licence and access costs would that require?

tasks.short: Help site managers match staffing needs with available people, skills, and certificates.

today.trigger: A site needs cover, peak-season capacity, a transfer, or a different mix of permanent and flex workers.
steps: Discuss required capacity and skills with the site manager.
Collect availability, contract hours, qualifications, and certificate status.
Check agency capacity and identify gaps or restrictions.
Compare staffing, training, overtime, and transfer options.
Agree the approach with managers and relevant employees, then coordinate implementation.
drudgery: Reconciling employee and agency lists.
Checking certificate expiry dates repeatedly.
Rebuilding the same staffing scenarios in Excel.
today.time_sinks: Availability and agency capacity change faster than the nightly Power BI extract, while certificate and contract information sit in different systems.

lenses.faster: A rules-based check combines capacity, contract constraints, and certificate validity into a gap list. Repeated reconciliation and spreadsheet scenario building disappear.
lenses.autonomous: Updated demand or staffing files rerun coverage and certificate checks and flag missing information. Managers still confirm live availability and approve individual assignments.
lenses.ambitious: Maintain a rolling capacity and training plan for all three sites before seasonal peaks arrive. Compare how permanent hiring, flex capacity, and cross-training affect continuity and cost.
lenses.joy: Remove list cleaning and repeated qualification checks. Keep discussing development opportunities and solving staffing problems with managers and employees.
lenses.options: Compare permanent hiring, agency cover, overtime, cross-training, and voluntary transfers with explicit costs and constraints.
lenses.altitude: Own the staffing rules and capability plan rather than manually assembling each staffing proposal.
reach: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: define capacity and qualification data requirements.
Learning and Development Specialist: prioritise training that closes verified coverage gaps.
FP&A Analyst: prepare staffing-cost assumptions and scenario inputs.
Site planners: prepare coverage options for their approval.

tasks.human_edge: Knowing whether a move is acceptable, safe, and fair requires conversations and operational judgment. Employees are not interchangeable capacity units.
tasks.pattern_why: deterministic_software checks explicit capacity, contract, and certificate constraints and calculates scenarios. A copilot explains aggregate trade-offs; it does not infer personality, rank workers, or decide assignments.

in_practice.trigger: A site manager changes the demand plan or an approved staffing or certificate extract is updated.
steps: Load dated demand, staffing, and qualification extracts and reject missing or inconsistent records.
Apply approved contract, working-time, rest, qualification, and certificate rules.
Calculate coverage gaps and several costed capacity scenarios without AI scores for individual workers.
The HRBP and site planner check live availability, employee preferences, and operational feasibility.
Managers approve assignments, transfers, training, or agency orders and record their reasons.
in_practice.human_gate: Managers and the HRBP approve individual changes; the planner owns the roster. Any extension to AI-based worker matching or performance scoring receives a separate legal classification and OR review.
systems: Approved exports from staffing agency portals
Power BI for dated aggregate trends
data_needed: Demand by site, shift, and required qualification.
Contract hours, verified availability, and working-time constraints.
Certificate validity dates and required qualifications.
Agency availability and agreed rates.
Employee-stated transfer or development preferences, with restricted access.
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint planning register: input timestamps, rule versions, gaps, scenario costs, approvals, and overrides. Individual assignment records remain in the authorised operational process.

evidence.claim: Microsoft describes its Workforce Insights agent as supporting questions about structure, staffing, workforce distribution, and hiring. This demonstrates information access rather than proven individual allocation outcomes.
AI that allocates work using individual behaviour or traits, or evaluates performance, falls within Annex III employment categories, subject to classification provisions.
evidence.source: [S9: EU AI Act, Annex III, section 4](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/annex/3/)

evidence.claim: The Commission confirms that Annex III high-risk obligations apply from 2 December 2027.
When applicable, Article 26 requires competent human oversight, worker information, and controlled system logs retained for at least six months unless applicable law provides otherwise.
The rules-based design, 30% labour saving, and 1.25 times elapsed speed are untested assumptions dependent on data quality and current roster access.

risks: Nightly dashboard data is too old to authorise same-day assignments.
Missing agency certificates or incomplete availability can create unsafe coverage assumptions.
A valid certificate does not establish practical readiness for every task or site.
Adding AI rankings or behaviour-based matching changes the legal and governance requirements; human approval alone does not remove high-risk classification.
The calculator must expose infeasible plans and binding constraints instead of presenting every scenario as workable.
research_questions: Where are authoritative live rosters and availability held, and can they be accessed lawfully?
Are certificate expiry dates complete for employees and all three agencies?
Can planners express the relevant CAO, rest, qualification, and operational constraints as testable rules?
Does a pilot reduce preparation time while maintaining safe coverage and acceptable employee outcomes?

tasks.short: Advise managers on hiring and retention plans that produce people who succeed and stay.

today.trigger: Vacancies remain open, offer acceptance falls, new hires leave early, or managers request a hiring or retention programme.
steps: Clarify the problem with the manager and Recruiter.
Collect recruitment, onboarding, training, retention, and cost information.
Compare sites and roles and listen to managers and recent hires.
Develop options with expected benefits, costs, and delivery requirements.
Agree owners and measures, then review results with management.
drudgery: Rebuilding vacancy and new-hire cohorts.
Joining recruitment records to employee records.
Preparing similar programme briefs and action trackers.
today.time_sinks: The company needs to connect hiring activity with week-one onboarding, actual productivity, and day-90 retention; no single system contains the whole outcome.

lenses.faster: Reusable cohort analysis assembles the facts and an AI draft turns them into a programme brief. Manual joining, repeated chart preparation, and first-draft writing shrink.
lenses.autonomous: A weekly refresh flags agreed aggregate changes in hiring, onboarding, and retention and drafts questions for the next manager review. It does not label individuals as likely leavers.
lenses.ambitious: Run small, measured improvements for each site and major role group instead of relying on an annual retention initiative. Follow every vacancy cohort through to productive employment at day 90.
lenses.joy: Remove spreadsheet preparation and repeated presentation drafting. Keep diagnosing the problem with managers and testing changes that improve employees' experience.
lenses.options: Compare buddy support, realistic job previews, shift arrangements, supervisor coaching, and certificate preparation with stated costs and assumptions.
lenses.altitude: Own the system of hiring and retention experiments, including outcome definitions and decisions to expand, adjust, or stop programmes.
reach: Recruiter: improve hiring-process design and manager readiness.
Learning and Development Specialist: coordinate onboarding experiments and supervisor learning.
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: define hiring cohorts and outcome measures.
FP&A Analyst: build programme-cost and capacity scenarios.

tasks.human_edge: The HRBP distinguishes a recruitment problem from an operational or management problem and gains commitment to changes that managers can actually deliver.
tasks.pattern_why: deterministic_software joins approved cohorts and calculates metrics; llm_step drafts a source-linked diagnosis and options. copilot keeps the HRBP responsible for causal interpretation, programme choice, and management advice.

in_practice.trigger: The weekly review date arrives or an agreed aggregate hiring or retention threshold is crossed.
steps: Join approved Recruitee, AFAS, and Studytube extracts using a verified hire-to-employee mapping.
Calculate vacancy-cohort outcomes and distinguish observed day-90 results from hires whose follow-up is incomplete.
Draft a brief separating findings, possible explanations, and information still needed.
The HRBP tests explanations through manager and employee conversations and develops costed options.
Management approves a bounded experiment with owners, comparison measures, and a review date.
in_practice.human_gate: The HRBP validates the diagnosis and recommendation; management approves expenditure and operational changes. Relevant personnel-policy changes go through the OR process before implementation.
systems: Approved enterprise LLM for briefs and options, proposed
data_needed: Vacancy IDs, offers, acceptances, start dates, and hire-to-employee mapping.
Week-one onboarding milestones.
Certificate completion and expiry information.
Manager-verified productive status and day-90 employment status.
Aggregate exit reasons and programme costs, separating permanent and agency cohorts.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint experiment register: metric definitions, extract dates, evidence, hypotheses, approved intervention, costs, owners, and review results.

evidence.claim: Connecting recruitment, employee, and learning records can support vacancy-cohort analysis, provided identifiers and outcome definitions are reliable.
Workday reports using a narrowly scoped Sana agent to generate tailored interview questions across its skills and roles. It does not establish improved 90-day retention.
evidence.source: [S2: Workday's HR workflows with Sana, vendor self-report](https://blog.workday.com/en-us/how-workdays-hr-team-is-reimagining-workflows-with-sana.html)

evidence.claim: A Danish study covering HR professionals and ten other occupations found average reported chatbot time savings of about 3%; this cautions against treating narrow preparation gains as whole-role results.
evidence.source: [S5: Humlum and Vestergaard, Large Language Models, Small Labor Market Effects](https://bfi.uchicago.edu/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/BFI_WP_2025-56-3.pdf)

evidence.claim: The 40% labour saving and 1.3 times elapsed speed apply to programme preparation and advice, not the time required to hire or establish retention outcomes.

risks: Certificate completion can be mistaken for productive performance; managers must verify readiness.
Seasonality, job mix, and agency composition can explain apparent programme effects.
Incomplete day-90 follow-up can distort the North Star if unresolved outcomes are omitted.
AI-generated explanations may turn correlations into causal claims.
Individual candidate scoring or employee flight-risk profiling would require a separate assessment; it is outside this design.
research_questions: Can hires be reliably linked from Recruitee to AFAS without including unrelated candidate records?
How will Noordhaven define and verify productive status for each major role?
Are cohort sizes sufficient to distinguish programme effects from seasonal changes?
Do managers implement the proposed changes, and do measured outcomes improve relative to a credible comparison?

tasks.short: Help managers interview well, give useful feedback, and document performance problems fairly.

today.trigger: A manager prepares for interviews, appraisal discussions, a difficult conversation, or documentation of performance concerns.
steps: Clarify the manager's situation and learning need.
Find approved guidance, interview criteria, and documentation templates.
Prepare examples or a training session for the relevant role and site.
Coach the manager and practise difficult parts of the conversation.
Review documentation and agree follow-up support or learning.
drudgery: Adapting the same training material for different managers.
Drafting interview questions from scratch.
Checking whether notes contain dates, examples, and agreed follow-up.
today.time_sinks: Preparation and template adaptation take time, while effective coaching still depends on the manager practising and receiving candid feedback.

lenses.faster: Generate role-specific interview questions, training examples, and documentation checklists from approved material. The HRBP edits a useful starting point instead of rebuilding each pack.
lenses.autonomous: A scheduled interview or appraisal can offer the manager an approved preparation pack and optional practice session. Personal performance conclusions are never generated or sent automatically.
lenses.ambitious: Offer every supervisor regular practice for interviewing and difficult conversations, including supervisors on evening and night shifts.
lenses.joy: Remove slide production and repetitive template checking. Keep candid coaching and helping managers speak clearly in their own words.
lenses.options: Provide several ways to open a conversation and practise different fictional responses. Show how wording can be specific and respectful without weakening the message.
lenses.altitude: Own manager capability standards and the practice system, using observed behaviour and employee feedback to improve the training.
reach: Learning and Development Specialist: build and maintain manager practice modules.
Recruiter: prepare structured interview guides with job-relevant criteria.
HR Administrator: check approved documentation for completeness.

tasks.human_edge: The HRBP challenges weak evidence, listens for unfair assumptions, and helps the manager take responsibility. The manager must own the conversation and its factual basis.
tasks.pattern_why: copilot drafts materials and supports practice while the HRBP leads coaching. deterministic_software checks document completeness; keep_human applies to appraisals, disciplinary judgments, and employment decisions.

in_practice.trigger: A manager requests support or receives an approved preparation prompt before an interview or appraisal.
steps: Select the approved module, role requirements, and relevant company guidance.
Generate a draft preparation pack using fictional examples or authorised, minimised facts.
The HRBP reviews questions, wording, and checks for job relevance and fairness.
The manager practises through a disclosed AI role-play or a live coaching session.
The HRBP reviews consequential documentation, and the manager confirms the factual record and follow-up.
in_practice.human_gate: The HRBP approves training packs and any documentation affecting employment. Managers verify every factual statement; legal advice is sought where the proposed action requires it.
systems: Recruitee role descriptions and interview criteria
Approved enterprise LLM or role-play service, proposed
data_needed: Job requirements and approved interview criteria.
Company feedback and documentation standards.
Relevant CAO and policy guidance.
Fictional practice scenarios.
Verified case facts only when necessary; no general mailbox or meeting surveillance.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint training library for approved materials and revisions; Studytube for completion records. Approved personal documentation enters the restricted employee file, with practice transcripts normally excluded.

evidence.claim: Workday reports that half of calibration-agent users cut preparation time by up to 75%; its check-in agent users improved feedback quality more than non-users. These are self-reported, context-specific findings.
Cornell's IBM exchange describes difficult-conversation role-play pilots, without demonstrated outcome improvements.
Using AI to evaluate employee performance or influence promotion or termination can fall within Annex III employment categories; a drafting-only design needs a documented intended-purpose assessment.
The 35% labour saving and 1.3 times elapsed speed are planning assumptions for preparation, adaptation, and checking, with live coaching retained.

risks: Generated notes can invent examples or make a weak dismissal file appear more complete than it is.
Managers may repeat language they cannot explain or defend, damaging trust.
Role-play must not infer emotions or personality from a manager's face or voice.
Coaching can drift into employee scoring or recommendations about dismissal, changing the system's risk classification.
A completed module does not establish that a manager can conduct a fair conversation.
research_questions: How much current time goes into material preparation versus live coaching?
Do managers produce more specific, factual documentation after using the support?
Do employees judge the resulting conversations clearer and fairer?
Can the service support practice without retaining personal case information or scoring employees?

tasks.short: Design ways to hear employee concerns and check whether working conditions and complaint routes are improving.

today.trigger: The HR Director or OR requests a listening programme, a policy change needs evaluation, or concerns arise about working conditions.
steps: Agree what the company needs to understand with the OR and site representatives.
Design survey questions, listening sessions, and accessible complaint routes.
Set confidentiality, ownership, reporting, and follow-up arrangements.
Pilot the approach across different sites and shifts.
Review participation and whether concerns lead to action, then adjust the method.
systems: AFAS Profit for limited workforce denominators
drudgery: Drafting several versions of similar questionnaires.
Rebuilding survey schedules and action trackers.
Reconciling response counts with site and shift populations.
today.time_sinks: The hard work is designing a credible listening process for office, frontline, and agency workers, then ensuring managers act on what people say.

lenses.faster: Draft neutral questions, language variants, sampling plans, and action templates from a clear brief. The HRBP spends more time checking trust and accessibility.
lenses.autonomous: Approved survey schedules, reminders, and aggregate participation checks run automatically. Formal complaints enter a separate confidential human process.
lenses.ambitious: Hear regularly from each shift and from flex workers, then show what changed because of their feedback. Measure whether complaint routes are usable as well as whether satisfaction rises.
lenses.joy: Remove questionnaire formatting and schedule administration. Keep listening to employees and persuading managers to fix the conditions causing concern.
lenses.options: Compare short pulse surveys, site roundtables, representative sampling, and confidential one-to-one routes before choosing a method.
lenses.altitude: Own the employee listening and response system, including representativeness, confidentiality, complaint handling, and visible action.
reach: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: define survey methodology and safe aggregation rules.
HR Administrator: coordinate survey distribution and action tracking.
HR Director: prepare evidence and options for OR discussions.
Site operations: organise follow-up on working-condition concerns.

tasks.human_edge: Employees must trust that raising a concern will not harm them and that someone will act. Method design and confidential complaint handling need accountable human ownership.
tasks.pattern_why: copilot helps design questions and methods; deterministic_software handles schedules and approved aggregation. keep_human applies to complaints, confidentiality choices, and decisions about remedial action.

in_practice.trigger: An approved listening cycle or policy-evaluation project begins.
steps: The HRBP and OR agree purpose, workforce coverage, confidentiality, and a separate formal complaint route.
Draft questions and language variants, then test them with representatives from sites, shifts, and agencies.
Approve the method, privacy basis, retention, reporting thresholds, and action owners before collecting responses.
Run approved distribution and reminders with accessible alternatives for employees without digital access.
Review aggregate participation and method quality, then publish agreed actions and human contact routes.
in_practice.human_gate: The HRBP approves the design with applicable OR consent and privacy review. A named human receives formal complaints and determines urgency, investigation, and protection measures.
systems: SharePoint for approved methods and action tracking
Microsoft 365 survey tooling, proposed with anonymity and access settings to verify
Excel and Power BI for aggregate participation checks
AFAS Profit and agency headcount extracts for limited denominators
data_needed: Workforce counts by site, shift, and employment category.
Approved questions and verified translations.
Accessible distribution routes and representative testing feedback.
Aggregation and disclosure-control rules.
Complaint owners, escalation arrangements, and action deadlines.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint method register: approved purpose, OR decisions, questionnaire versions, privacy settings, participation checks, and actions. Identifiable complaints are stored separately with restricted access.

evidence.claim: Cornell's exchange recommends combining employee conversations and other feedback mechanisms, including attention to differences between corporate and plant workers.
Workplace biometric emotion inference is prohibited under Article 5(1)(f), subject to medical or safety exceptions; satisfaction measurement does not justify it.
SER describes OR rights concerning AI-related personnel-policy changes and employee monitoring.
The 25% labour saving and 1.15 times elapsed speed are untested design-and-administration estimates; consultation and trust building remain.

risks: Small groups or distinctive free-text details can reveal identities despite removing names.
Office employees may dominate results if warehouse shifts and agency workers lack access or time.
Passive analysis of Teams messages would introduce monitoring and privacy issues; it is outside this voluntary listening design.
Participation being voluntary does not automatically make employee consent a suitable GDPR lawful basis.
A survey is not a substitute for an urgent complaint route or a legally required reporting procedure.
research_questions: Which sites, shifts, languages, and agency groups are missing from existing feedback?
Can anonymity claims be supported by actual survey settings, metadata handling, and reporting controls?
Will employees use the proposed complaint routes without fearing retaliation?
Do managers close agreed actions, and do employees recognise the resulting changes?

tasks.short: Report what employees say about work and which management actions need attention.

today.trigger: A survey cycle ends or management requests an update on employee satisfaction and related issues.
steps: Collect approved survey results, complaint aggregates, and action updates.
Clean the data and calculate response rates and comparable results.
Read comments and identify themes without exposing individuals.
Build charts and a presentation explaining findings and limitations.
Check the report, present it, and record management actions.
drudgery: Copying numbers and charts into slides.
Repeatedly grouping similar comments.
Checking denominators and updating the same narrative.
today.time_sinks: Manual comment coding and presentation preparation take time; the final report still needs checks for privacy, comparability, and unsupported conclusions.

lenses.faster: Refresh approved calculations and charts automatically, then draft a narrative from checked aggregates and coded comments. Copying, first-pass comment grouping, and routine slide writing largely disappear.
lenses.autonomous: A validated dataset triggers a draft management pack with freshness, response-rate, and disclosure checks. The report is released only after HRBP approval.
lenses.ambitious: Provide timely, safe feedback for sites and shifts and track whether management actions changed employees' experience. Keep the reporting frequency proportionate to participation and usefulness.
lenses.joy: Remove chart copying and repetitive coding. Keep explaining what matters and securing commitment to specific actions.
lenses.options: Produce an executive brief, a site discussion pack, and a workforce summary from the same approved facts.
lenses.altitude: Own reporting definitions, disclosure rules, interpretation standards, and the connection between findings and management action.
reach: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: maintain business definitions and report specifications.
HR Administrator: consolidate action status and reporting inputs.
Controller or FP&A Analyst: add reviewed cost assumptions to proposed improvements.

tasks.human_edge: The HRBP checks whether the report fairly represents minority concerns and explains uncertainty. Management needs accountable interpretation, especially when findings challenge its behaviour.
tasks.pattern_why: deterministic_software calculates metrics and disclosure controls; llm_step groups redacted comments and drafts text. agent_with_gate assembles the report across sources and requires approval before publication.

in_practice.trigger: Approved survey data arrives or the scheduled reporting date is reached.
steps: Validate input dates, denominators, response counts, and comparability against the approved method.
Calculate metrics and enforce minimum-group and secondary-suppression rules before creating report outputs.
Redact identifying comment details and propose theme codes with traceable restricted references.
Generate charts and draft commentary distinguishing findings, uncertainty, and proposed actions.
The HRBP reviews figures, themes, disclosure risk, and narrative, then approves publication to authorised audiences.
in_practice.human_gate: Every management or workforce report requires HRBP approval. The People Analytics and HRIS Analyst validates changed metric logic; identifiable complaints never enter the reporting model.
systems: SharePoint restricted source and publication libraries
Proposed workflow automation and approved enterprise LLM for redacted comment coding and drafting
data_needed: Approved survey responses and workforce denominators.
Restricted, redacted free-text comments.
Reporting definitions and disclosure-control rules.
Comparable prior-period results.
Aggregate complaint measures and approved management action status.
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint reporting register: dataset versions, refresh results, suppression checks, comment-code review, generated drafts, corrections, approval, and published version.

evidence.claim: Power BI supports dashboards that present consolidated visual information; Noordhaven already uses it for HR and finance reporting.
Power BI reports can be embedded in SharePoint Online while retaining Power BI access requirements.
evidence.source: [Microsoft Learn: Embed a Power BI report in SharePoint Online](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/collaborate-share/office-integration/service-embed-report-spo)

evidence.claim: An LLM can propose themes and draft narratives from redacted comments and checked aggregates, but reliable interpretation and privacy controls require local validation.
The 65% labour saving and 2.5 times elapsed speed assume reusable calculations and templates, sufficient comment volume, and a short approval cycle.

risks: A minimum group size alone does not prevent identification through cross-filtering, comparisons, or distinctive comments.
AI summaries can understate rare but serious concerns or misread comments in different languages.
Changing questions or workforce composition can invalidate trend comparisons.
The nightly AFAS refresh must be shown explicitly; figures are not live workforce counts.
Reports must not rank individual employees or infer satisfaction from personal communications.
research_questions: How much reporting time is spent on calculations, comment coding, slides, approval, and presentation?
Does reviewed comment coding preserve serious minority themes across languages?
Can report permissions and disclosure controls prevent identification through combined filters and outputs?
Does the draft reproduce checked figures correctly and lead to clearer, completed management actions?

role.altitude: The HRBP becomes the owner of manager capability, fair case resolution, and improvements from vacancy to productive employment at day 90. Routine information services supply answers and evidence; the HRBP designs their boundaries and uses the resulting capacity for conversations and operational change.
reach: HR Administrator: oversee intake, case completeness, and follow-up rules.
Recruiter: improve manager interviewing and hiring-to-onboarding handoffs.
Learning and Development Specialist: design supervisor practice and target training at verified capability gaps.
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: own business questions, outcome definitions, and interpretation while the analyst owns technical data quality.
Compensation and Benefits Specialist: improve explanations of approved terms and identify issues needing specialist review.
FP&A Analyst and Controller: prepare workforce and programme-cost scenarios for finance validation.
Site managers and planners: facilitate staffing and retention improvements while operational leaders retain assignment authority.
role.ceiling_note: These seven tasks cover about 49.9% of the supplied role time. The untested estimates total about 336 hours per HRBP annually, or 1,009 hours across 3 FTE, worth roughly EUR 80,700 of gross capacity at EUR 80/hour. That is about 21% of total role time, before implementation, licences, maintenance, and additional service demand; it is not a cash-saving or headcount forecast. Savings use distinct task buckets so the shared policy service is counted once. Speedup estimates concern each task from trigger to completed output, including remaining human and automated work; consultation and operational waits limit elapsed gains. Trust, conflict resolution, medical boundaries, CAO interpretation, OR rights, and employment accountability limit autonomy. Qualifying employment AI remains subject to high-risk obligations from 2 December 2027, and human approval does not by itself remove that classification.
skills_to_grow: Maintain approved policy sources and translate applicability rules into testable workflows.
Evaluate answer accuracy, escalation quality, and differences across worker groups and languages.
Understand AVG/GDPR, OR consultation and consent rights, and AI Act intended-purpose classification.
Coach managers using practice, observed behaviour, and employee feedback.
Define vacancy cohorts, productive status, and credible programme comparisons.
Read workforce-cost scenarios and challenge weak assumptions with finance and operations.
Design accessible services for shift workers and agency workers while preserving human contact.
role.ambitious_version: Keep a named HRBP relationship for each site while sharing specialisms across the three-person team. Give employees accessible policy help and reliable human escalation, offer every supervisor regular coaching practice, and run measured hiring, onboarding, and working-condition improvements by site and role. Judge success through vacancy cohorts that produce hires who are productive and still employed after 90 days, supported by week-one onboarding, offer acceptance, absence, and manager satisfaction. Track unresolved issues and days to resolution alongside service usage so faster answers translate into better outcomes.
